runs.title: HTTP caching basics — dated baseline
runs.summary: Established the dated standards-grounded baseline for freshness and reuse, stale responses, conditional validation, private versus shared storage, and common Cache-Control mistakes.

runs.title: Follow-up: ETag versus Last-Modified precedence
runs.summary: Added the narrow validator comparison: If-None-Match wins, a nonmatching ETag prevents date fallback, and the curl matrix is expected rather than measured because curl was unavailable.

runs.title: Cache-key & privacy mismatch
runs.summary: Added the query, Vary, Cookie, Set-Cookie, and Authorization worksheet, separated expected protocol outcomes from a local key/match model, and documented why no live shared-cache measurement is claimed.

runs.title: Locating the serving layer
runs.summary: Added the expected layer-attribution path, browser/worker/history/intermediary/origin comparison matrices, a decision tree, diagnostic checklist, and explicit limits; no live shared-cache capture is claimed.

runs.title: CloudFront TTL policy and invalidation — audit refresh
runs.summary: Refreshed the preserved CloudFront report URL with the completed 19 Sep audit: s-maxage-only documentation gap, viewer-only response-headers policy boundary, effective cache-key invalidation scope, rewrite-stage limits, and Completed-status evidence. No live CloudFront measurement or invalidation was performed.

runs.title: Cloudflare Cache Rules and Origin Cache Control
runs.summary: Added a documentation-grounded Cloudflare case covering OCC and Cache Rule edge precedence, separate Browser TTL, cache-key identity, purge scopes, a matched CloudFront crosswalk, and an authorized-only verification template. No Cloudflare zone response or purge was available.

runs.title: Cache deployment and incident runbook
runs.summary: Added a provider-neutral checklist for private/sensitive and public/versioned responses, a symptom-first incident path, named-hop evidence sequence, versioned URL versus named-provider purge guidance, separate CloudFront and Cloudflare sidebars, and explicit downstream limits. Documentation-only; no live provider capture was available.

runs.title: When stale HTTP content is allowed
runs.summary: Separated storage, freshness, bounded stale permission, and validation; added a browser/shared timing example, directive matrix, symptom-first paths, named-hop evidence limits, safe private/public/versioned guardrails, and an authorized-only test matrix. Documentation-only; no live result is claimed.

runs.title: Service-worker updates and stale client assets
runs.summary: Separated specified update/install/wait/activate transitions, skipWaiting() and clients.claim(), current document code, and Cache Storage cleanup. Added a conservative compatible rollout and expected/unexecuted diagnostics. Documentation-only; no browser, application, origin, or lifecycle result is claimed.

runs.title: HTTP redirect caching and stale route targets
runs.summary: Added per-hop redirect response and Location guidance, status/method/cacheability comparison, bounded route policy choices, and an expected/unexecuted symptom checklist. No live route, browser, provider, or cache result is claimed.

runs.title: Browser HTTP-cache partitioning: context is not policy
runs.summary: Separated the Fetch partition model from RFC 9111 cache matching and policy, compared Chrome/Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit documentation, and showed why browser partitioning does not control shared intermediaries or replace private/no-store policy. Context examples are expected, not tested; no browser or cache result is claimed.

runs.title: Request-side HTTP cache controls
runs.summary: Compared six RFC 9111 request Cache-Control directives with response policy and explained why request preferences are advisory—not universal bypass, origin-contact, purge, or privacy commands. The examples are synthetic standards expectations; no authorized runtime or browser/provider experiment was available.

runs.title: POST response caching and unsafe-request invalidation
runs.summary: Separated POST-specific response eligibility—explicit freshness and same-target Content-Location, with possible later GET/HEAD reuse—from unsafe-request write-through and 2xx/3xx target-URI invalidation at traversed caches. The matrix is expected and unexecuted; no implementation result is claimed.

runs.title: Negative caching of missing versioned assets
runs.summary: Added the standards-level boundary for 404/410 responses: heuristically cacheable does not mean stored, and status alone supplies no lifetime. A stored negative response may remain reusable after bytes return at the same URI; a new no-store response is not a purge. The report also distinguishes named HTTP-cache evidence from service-worker or application responses. Documentation-only; no implementation result is claimed.

runs.title: How Age relates to current_age
runs.summary: Explained RFC 9111 §4.2.3’s initial-age choices and resident-time calculation, the generated Age requirement for unvalidated stored-response reuse, and the limits of Age as hop evidence. The arithmetic is fully synthetic; no live cache behavior was tested.

runs.title: Authorization reuse and proxy-revalidate
runs.summary: RFC 9111 §3.5 lists must-revalidate, public, and s-maxage as permissions for a shared cache to reuse a response to an Authorization request; proxy-revalidate instead governs validation before stale reuse. Erratum 9004 proposed a no-behavior-change clarification, but its final disposition was not confirmed from the accessible archive record. No cache implementation behavior was tested.

runs.title: Selecting stored responses after a 304
runs.summary: Added a standards-based 304 candidate and validator-selection guide. Strong validators select all matches; weak validators select the most recent matching response only when no strong validator is present; the no-validator case is limited to one validator-less candidate. A 304 updates metadata rather than carrying replacement bytes. The example is synthetic; no implementation behavior was tested.

runs.title: CDN-targeted Cache-Control
runs.summary: Explained RFC 9213 target-list selection and fallback, distinguished targeted fields from ordinary shared-cache s-maxage, and summarized Cloudflare’s documented precedence and forwarding. The comparison is synthetic; no implementation, zone, endpoint, browser, or cache was tested.
